item.title: For investors, the Iran war redefined energy security
item.description:
Nearly eight months of war in Iran have produced one of the most severe energy shocks in decades, exposing a sharp divide between the countries that absorbed it with surprising ease and those forced into painful tradeoffs. Resilience, it turns out, comes less from any single technology or policy than from systems-level thinking, long-term investment, and deliberate planning. The countries that coped best were not always those with the most energy resources. They were the ones that had built flexibility, redundancy, and alternative pathways into their energy systems. China drew on strategic reserves, alternative pipeline imports, and fuel switching. The US benefited from record domestic oil and gas production, regional storage and solar to improve summer grid stability, and secure North American supply chains.
